##  {#welcome data-menu-title="Welcome"}

[Welcome!]{.slide-title}

::: body-text
**Instructors:** Dr. Gretchen LeBuhn & Dr. Nicole Adelstein

**Today's Focus:** Thinking clearly about data

**What to expect:** - Get to know each other - Surface big ideas in data science - Establish course norms
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#what-this-is data-menu-title="What This Course Is"}

[What This Course Is About]{.slide-title}

::: body-text
This is a course about **thinking clearly with data**.

**Not about:** - Being a coder already - Memorizing functions - Learning statistics in isolation

**About:** - Explaining your reasoning - Spotting your assumptions - Revising when things don't make sense
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#prior-experience data-menu-title="Prior Experience"}

[You Belong Here]{.slide-title}

::: body-text
**Prior coding experience is not what matters.**

What matters: - Willingness to ask "why" - Explaining your choices - Revising when things are unclear

**That's science. We're applying it to data work.**
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#today-plan data-menu-title="Today's Plan"}

[How Today Will Work]{.slide-title}

::: body-text
1.  **Get to know each other** through noticing patterns in data

2.  **Surface big data science ideas** without code

3.  **Talk about norms** for working together

**I'm noticing *how* you think, not *what* you already know.**
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#ambiguity data-menu-title="Ambiguity"}

[Ambiguity in "Data"]{.slide-title}

::: body-text
Some people answered with:

\- **Format**

\- **Content**

\- **Collection method**

**The ambiguity doesn't go away when you start coding.**

It just gets buried under syntax.

**The hardest part of data science?** Deciding what you're even measuring.
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#class-dataset data-menu-title="Class as Dataset"}

[This Class as a Dataset]{.slide-title}

::: body-text
**Breakout Activity (10 minutes):**

Imagine describing this class as a dataset for someone who wasn't here.

-   What **variables** would you include?
-   How would you **define** them?
-   What information do you **wish you had**?

**Write your reasoning**, not just a list.

Google Doc link in chat →
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

:::

##  {#experience-example data-menu-title="Experience Example"}

[Example: Measuring "Experience"]{.slide-title}

::: body-text
"Experience" could mean:

\- Time in grad program

\- Prior statistics courses

\- Comfort with ambiguity

\- Years working with data

**You didn't fail because you couldn't agree.**

You succeeded because you **noticed the decision you'd have to make.**

**That's data science.**
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#what-we-did data-menu-title="What We Did"}

[What We Just Did]{.slide-title}

::: body-text
Without writing a single line of code, you:

✓ Defined variables

✓ Noticed ambiguity

✓ Made decisions and justified them

✓ Realized others might make different decisions

**This is the foundation of everything we'll do this semester.**
:::

##  {#course-norms data-menu-title="Course Norms"}

[Course Norms]{.slide-title}

::: body-text
**My commitments to you:**

1.  I will not assume you know things
2.  I will not mistake speed for understanding
3.  I will not treat "I don't know" as failure
4.  I will give you time to think
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#your-norms data-menu-title="Your Commitments"}

[What I Need From You]{.slide-title}

::: body-text
1.  **Ask questions out loud** — if you're confused, someone else is too

2.  **Try things when you're not sure** — messy reasoning \> polished guessing

3.  **Be kind** to each other and yourselves
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#your-goals data-menu-title="Your Goals"}

[Your Turn]{.slide-title}

::: {.body-text .center-text}
**Two questions** (chat or unmute):

1.  What do you want to accomplish this semester?

2.  What do you need from me or from each other to make that happen?
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#themes data-menu-title="Themes"}

What I think I'm hearing

::: body-text
-   You want to feel **competent**, not just compliant

-   You want to **understand**, not just copy

-   You want **space to struggle** without judgment

**We can work with that.**
:::

##  {#before-wednesday data-menu-title="Before Wednesday"}

[Before Wednesday]{.slide-title}

::: body-text
**Think about this question:**

What decisions did we make today that felt invisible at the time?

We're not writing code yet, but we're already making choices about what counts, what matters, and how to define things.
:::

[Final Thought]{.slide-title}

::: {.body-text .center-text}
Everything we did today — thinking, struggling with definitions, noticing ambiguity —

**That's not "pre-data-science."**

**That IS data science.**

**The thinking is the work.**
